meta.title: CivicOS experience inputs for UX design
readThis: Every line carries basis. 'fixed' means the canon or the approved module requirements say it, and src names where. 'open' means the canon does not settle it; the text is the question the design must answer. Nothing marked open has an invented answer.

Act references use the inventory's own names, written 'construct-id: Act name' (docs/development/ux-substrate/ux-substrate.json). Screen inventory, act weights and working names are another worker's job and are not repeated here.

Two words mean two things. RUNG is how heavy an act is (reversible, reasoned, terminal, attested, irreversible). WEIGHT is how an act applied to a set behaves (refuse = all or nothing, report = proceed and say what moved, per-item = each applied or kept with its reason, single = one object). Source: affordances R1-R2; Interaction Constructs, naming collision corrected 2026-08-01.

'Finding' is overloaded: in case-making it is a concluded question; in the queue it is a class of item the record noticed and nobody has judged (inventory contradictions). This file says 'concluded finding' or 'queue finding' where it matters.
Coverage (useCases) says whether approved module requirements (build/requirements/*.md) hold the use case, not whether it is built.

useCases.name: Search the record
useCases.goal: Find documents, passages, questions and legs by typing one query language.
useCases.trigger: A member wants something already held.
useCases.outcome: Rows the viewer may see, with facets, a note of what could not be seen, and widening when an AND finds nothing.

useCases.name: Search outside sources in one query (city data, legal databases, other groups, news)
useCases.goal: One question fans out to heterogeneous public sources with provenance and trust on each result.
useCases.trigger: A member does not yet hold the material.
useCases.outcome: Results with provenance, recency and trust signals, accepted into the record.
useCases.requirementIds: ai-runs R9-R14 (FIND only inside a run); capture-requests R1-R22
useCases.src: Functional Architecture 'Search across heterogeneous sources'; AI Roles section 2 (standalone FIND ABSENT)
useCases.coverageNote: No module holds a standalone fan-out search over outside sources; FIND exists only inside an investigative run.

useCases.outcome: Stage 1, documentation.

useCases.outcome: A sent entry on the action; blanks visible as [UNFILLED]; Tier 2 carries the advisory note.

journeyExperience.journey: (a) A group sets up and invites members
journeyExperience.spans: days; several people (operator, founder, second administrator, members)

steps.step: Install the signed release into the group's account
steps.whatTheyKnow: Needs a paid account with a payment method; the page states prerequisites.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Which slug to use (written once, public forever) and which jurisdiction profiles to offer.
whatCanGoWrong: Existing copy for the slug: refused, nothing changed (installer R5).
No payment method: refused, saying nothing was created (installer R4, R7).
Account already holds a copy: refused until installs are isolated (installer R32).
A part not serving the release: named, not claimed as done (installer R15, R33).
steps.howLong: One sitting; up to ten self-test tries.
steps.feelingRisk: The slug is public and permanent; a group wanting anonymity must choose an unrevealing one now.
steps.src: installer R2-R16, R21-R24, R32-R33; Publication section 7 point 1
openInThisStep: How the operator is told, in plain words, that the slug is permanent and public at the moment of choosing.

steps.step: Open the setup page and claim with the one-time password
steps.whatTheyKnow: Holds the password (the link may carry it as #boot=).
steps.decisionTheyMake: Choose a password of at least 12 characters.
whatCanGoWrong: The page could not read the group: says so, never 'none recorded' (instance-setup R20).
steps.feelingRisk: The founder becomes the root of trust with no custody model (DEC-2 deferred).
steps.src: membership R1; instance-setup R20-R22; control-plane R15

steps.step: Set display name, domain and jurisdiction profiles
steps.whatTheyKnow: The slug; the held profiles by name and coverage.
steps.decisionTheyMake: What the group calls itself; which domain to claim; which profiles (none preselected).
whatCanGoWrong: Domain verdict absent, mismatched or UNDETERMINED: not shown publicly; members see the state (instance-setup R8-R10).
Changing profiles changes how local facts read (warning; instance-setup R15).
steps.feelingRisk: Showing an unverified domain would claim an association the record cannot support.

steps.step: Add a second administrator (direct while fewer than two)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The floor is two administrators.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Who, with what cover (not a legal name).
whatCanGoWrong: Cover typed as a legal name defeats the protection (Membership v2 section 3).
steps.howLong: Minutes; then waits for the invitee.
steps.feelingRisk: Cover invites a legal name if the field is worded badly.

steps.step: Record who holds hosting access
steps.whoIsActing: the group, asked when the second administrator is added
steps.whatTheyKnow: Hosting access is outside the app.
whatCanGoWrong: Left unanswered: the record keeps whatever answer was given.
steps.feelingRisk: None named in canon.
openInThisStep: What the group is told about why this matters (the hosting account is the remedy against the founder).

steps.step: Add members with capabilities (default contribute)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Capabilities: contribute, publish, create_projects.
whatCanGoWrong: At two or more administrators, a new administrator is only proposed and needs a ballot (membership R14).
steps.handoffTo: invitee (burner URL sent by a channel the system does not record)
steps.feelingRisk: None named.
steps.src: membership R9, R12-R15; Membership v2 section 6

steps.step: Open the link, choose handle and password
steps.whatTheyKnow: Sees cover, role, capabilities and expertise; never the member id.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Handle (public in the record) and password.
whatCanGoWrong: NO_SUCH_INVITATION (spent or never existed, one answer).
steps.howLong: Minutes; the link is spent on use.
steps.feelingRisk: The handle is what the public sees; the member may not realise.

steps.step: Create a project with an objective
steps.whatTheyKnow: A project name is unique across the instance.
whatCanGoWrong: A project with no objective is refused (intent R1).
steps.feelingRisk: Members may believe projects are private; visibility is organisation, not secrecy.
steps.src: promotion R19; intent R1; membership R71; Membership v2 section 2

steps.step: Invite participants; they join
steps.whatTheyKnow: Handles.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Make the project discoverable; an outsider requests to join; owner grants
steps.whatTheyKnow: Outsiders see the name only.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Whether to expose the name; whether to grant.
whatCanGoWrong: A grant invites; the requester still has to join (membership R51).
steps.feelingRisk: Exposing a name tells every member the project exists.

journeyExperience.journey: (b) From a question to a published case
journeyExperience.spans: weeks; several members, possibly an outside reviewer

steps.step: Capture a public document
steps.whatTheyKnow: An address.
whatCanGoWrong: HOST_COOLING_OFF: the governor paces the host (capture R7).
Source refused or fetch failed, recorded as such (capture R8).
Rendered content UNDETERMINED; archive capture at most C.
steps.howLong: Seconds to minutes; renders may be deferred.
steps.feelingRisk: A capture is not evidence until a member stands behind it; the grade note may be discarded before the member sees it (DEC-51).
steps.src: capture R2-R18; AI Roles rule 4; DEC-51

steps.step: Release it (vouch for it)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Must see the source material itself, never only an AI summary.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Stand behind it, with acknowledgement and mitigation for a bulk release.
whatCanGoWrong: Refused with offenders named (weight refuse: all or nothing).
A second member released first: CAS_STALE (promotion R1).
steps.feelingRisk: Click-through bulk release would make the acknowledgement dishonest.
steps.src: UI-KICKOFF item 2; Interaction Constructs section J; affordances R1-R2
openInThisStep: No owning module requirement holds release (inFlux).

steps.step: Resolve its references to subjects
steps.whatTheyKnow: Recognised references with grades.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Accept matches; testify a missed one (grade D).
whatCanGoWrong: Ambiguous alias kept, never resolved silently (entities R6).
A C match never reads established.
steps.feelingRisk: One click from an established resolution off a machine-composed list (DEC-53).

steps.step: Open a question (or the assistant surfaces one)
steps.whatTheyKnow: What they want to know.
whatCanGoWrong: Surfaced by the assistant: must look surfaced; ages to deferred if nobody acts (intent R17).
steps.howLong: Minutes; ageing interval set per instance.
steps.feelingRisk: A machine question must not read as a member's obligation (D-82).
steps.src: inquiry R1-R2; ai-runs R25-R27; intent R16-R17

steps.step: Cite documents, passages or questions as supporting or cutting against
steps.whatTheyKnow: Earned grades per target.
whatCanGoWrong: A grouped question refuses a new leg until ungrouped (DEC-50).
A newer capture may exist: stale version notice.
steps.feelingRisk: Stating a grade the record did not earn: the leg is capped and why is shown.

steps.step: Open an assistant run to check or investigate
steps.whatTheyKnow: The run's bounds, lens and bar are recorded at open.
whatCanGoWrong: A bound stops the run and the log says which.
Capture requests wait on the daemon (hours).
steps.feelingRisk: The assistant appearing to conclude; transcripts are notes, never record.
steps.src: ai-runs R9-R24, R40; AI Roles section 3

steps.step: Accept a version (after the shared-origin check)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Versions with legs and per-axis strength; suggested ones labelled.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Accept, reject, consider, revert; preview first.
whatCanGoWrong: VERSION_* refusals; MACHINE_CANNOT_MOVE_VERSION for a machine.
steps.feelingRisk: Accepting a machine suggestion without reading it (DEC-68: the record cannot tell).

steps.step: Make it current for the project
steps.whatTheyKnow: Which version is accepted.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Which account the project stands on.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Conclude, stating what would falsify it (or that nothing would)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The current version and its strength.
whatCanGoWrong: Another project concluded differently: both stances stand.
steps.feelingRisk: False certainty: a falsifier of 'none' must be the member's stated override.

steps.step: Check strength against the bar; clear hunches
steps.whatTheyKnow: Per-axis pair per load-bearing finding; the project bar.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Which findings are load-bearing; which hunches to clear.
whatCanGoWrong: BELOW_PROJECT_STRENGTH naming member, axis, required and reached (case-authoring R6).
steps.howLong: Days if more evidence is needed.
steps.feelingRisk: Over-claiming: a case over an uncleared hunch states a strength that is not true.
steps.src: case-authoring R6, R12; strength R5; DEC-20

steps.step: Draft a review copy; grant outside reviewers
steps.whatTheyKnow: The copy is complete as a publication can be and names what is missing.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Whom to grant; when to revoke.
whatCanGoWrong: Grant dies if the draft moves case identity (review R8).
Recipient sees findings as the last editor could, absent ones by role only.
steps.feelingRisk: Calling it 'pre-publish' asserts a future that may not happen.

steps.step: Prepare the case: scope, statement, exclusions, bias acknowledgement
steps.whatTheyKnow: Concluded findings; the searched section computed from the log.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Roles, scope, what is left out and why.
steps.feelingRisk: Nothing may draft framing for the member (Case Making section 4a).

steps.step: Acknowledge the exclusion statement
steps.whoIsActing: joined participant or review recipient (not its writer)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The statement, shown first.
steps.feelingRisk: A gate pushing a one-person group to recruit a signature would be a bug; nobody-but-author is disclosed, not refused.

steps.step: Sign the case (own session, attesting key)
steps.whatTheyKnow: What becomes permanent and what it does and does not claim.
whatCanGoWrong: CASE_RATIFY_STALE (an acknowledgement or edit re-authored it).
steps.howLong: Minutes; the ceremony itself is deferred (DEC-33).
steps.feelingRisk: A member who thinks they certify authenticity has been misled (Interaction Constructs section A).
openInThisStep: The five-step ceremony and its pre-flight are deferred; only a placeholder surface is owed.

steps.step: Ratify each finding and its evidence
steps.whatTheyKnow: Pinned members awaiting signature.
whatCanGoWrong: A finding ratified before its evidence does not link to it on the published graph (Publication section 3 rule 2 gap).
steps.feelingRisk: Irreversible: correction only by a new edition.

steps.step: Read and verify by hash
steps.whatTheyKnow: No account.
whatCanGoWrong: A finding pinned by several cases: the reader chooses (FINDING_IN_SEVERAL_CASES).
Cases disagree on a finding's pair: CASES_DISAGREE, each case's pair shown.
steps.feelingRisk: Reading strength as a single score, or authenticity into a hash.

journeyExperience.spans: weeks to months; statutory clocks; several members; outside offices and counsel

steps.step: Declare the standard (or adopt a proposal)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The standard's captured text; profile source match.
whatCanGoWrong: Source undetermined when the profile does not supply it.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Record a determination per standard
steps.whatTheyKnow: Published findings with frozen pairs; standards in force.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Compliant, noncompliant or unclear, per standard.
whatCanGoWrong: A standard not in force at the act's date: refused.
Any significance, rank or score key: refused (R8).
basis_changed later when a finding reopens.
steps.feelingRisk: Judging significance through policy preference (Functional Architecture Function 4).

steps.step: Record consequences
steps.whatTheyKnow: What the record can compute; what must be assessed.
whatCanGoWrong: A part naming an individual: refused.
steps.feelingRisk: Composing harm into one headline figure (refused).

steps.step: Open an escalation
steps.whatTheyKnow: The determination is live and noncompliant.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Create a breach action to the office; set the risk tier
steps.whatTheyKnow: Counterparty by role and body from the profile.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Tier 1, 2 or 3 with a reason; governing laws.
whatCanGoWrong: LEASE_HELD (another member acting on the action).
steps.feelingRisk: Legally unsophisticated filing creating adverse precedent (Tier 3).

steps.step: Prepare, approve and record the filing sent
steps.whatTheyKnow: Draft with [UNFILLED] blanks; Tier 2 advisory first.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Approve text (edited or not); send outside the system; record sent.
whatCanGoWrong: FILING_STALE (tier, counterparty, determination or laws changed).
steps.howLong: Hours to send; then the clock.
steps.feelingRisk: A machine-prepared filing mistaken for the group's approved words.

steps.step: State the deadline with its legal basis
steps.whatTheyKnow: Profile deadlines, holidays.
whatCanGoWrong: Every date carries its statute; overdue is derived, never silently stale (actions R35).
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: The plane marks overdue and proposes the next stage
steps.whatTheyKnow: Clock dates; responses.
whatCanGoWrong: Not yet built: overdue marks and escalation prompts (monitoring R34-R35).
steps.feelingRisk: The system appearing to decide the next stage.
steps.src: monitoring R34-R35, R44; escalation R2, R16-R17

steps.step: Evaluate the response
steps.whatTheyKnow: Ledger entries; captured response.
steps.decisionTheyMake: complied / partial / denied / none, with reason.
whatCanGoWrong: Response arrives outside the system and must be captured.
Partial compliance does not stop the clock.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Advance to legal tools or political accountability
steps.whatTheyKnow: Proposed edges with triggers.
steps.feelingRisk: Advocacy creeping in: stage 7 only enforces an existing requirement.

steps.step: Assemble a counsel packet (Tier 3)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Six sections from the record.
steps.feelingRisk: A packet read as legal advice or as fileable.

steps.step: Record consequences addressed; end the escalation
steps.whatTheyKnow: Later compliant determination; addressed consequences.
steps.feelingRisk: Ending early; the exit condition is specific (Operational Principle 6).

journeyExperience.src: inventory journey (c); layer 9 modules; Design Requirements 7-8

steps.step: Open the queue
steps.whatTheyKnow: Obligations, then queue findings, then conditions, grouped by case.
whatCanGoWrong: Home set UNDETERMINED: an ancestor out of view or past the depth bound (stated, never named).
NO_CLASS / NO_SUCH_KIND: the whole feed refused.
steps.feelingRisk: A truncated set indistinguishable from nobody caring (DEC-16).

steps.step: See each item's options with rung and weight, pre-flighted
steps.whatTheyKnow: Only acts this caller can take.
whatCanGoWrong: An option that would be refused NO_PROJECT_SCOPE should not be offered (queue R18).
steps.feelingRisk: A surface guessing a refusal is worse than no pre-flight.
steps.src: queue R12, R17; affordances R11; DEC-8

steps.step: Resolve or forward obligations (as a set)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The obligation and who it is with.
whatCanGoWrong: Per-item: some retained with their reasons.
steps.feelingRisk: Silent disappearance for the member who did not resolve it (R39 not yet met).

steps.step: Defer or dismiss a queue finding, with a reason, for a project
steps.whatTheyKnow: Its source and derivation (never reads as an obligation).
steps.feelingRisk: Presenting machine findings as obligations (D-79 drowning).

steps.step: Take up an objective gap or proposal
steps.whatTheyKnow: The gap and what it would take.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Adopt, open a question, defer, dismiss.
whatCanGoWrong: Machine refused every adopt act (intent R20).
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Adopt newer or keep earlier on a version notice
steps.whatTheyKnow: Affected or undetermined grading of the newer capture.
steps.feelingRisk: Silence must be earned: never 'unaffected' unless read.

steps.step: Resolve a bias debt with a reason
steps.whatTheyKnow: Which lens moved.
steps.feelingRisk: Nagging: the debt is disclosed and blocks nothing.

steps.step: Mute a condition or snooze a case
steps.whatTheyKnow: Personal only.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Mute item, mute case kinds, snooze until.
steps.feelingRisk: A mute becoming a permanent blindfold; new kinds surface again.

steps.step: Mint a member-scoped AI credential
steps.whatTheyKnow: Its scope and principal.
steps.feelingRisk: The credential appearing to carry the member's capabilities (it holds none).
steps.src: membership R28-R30, R62; Membership v2 section 5

steps.step: Work the objective
steps.whatTheyKnow: The gaps.
steps.feelingRisk: The machine choosing the question.

steps.step: Run requests captures
steps.whatTheyKnow: Public addresses only.
whatCanGoWrong: CAPTURE_REQUEST_* refusals; body fields claiming bytes refused (capture-requests R4).
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Daemon drains requests under conduct rules
steps.whatTheyKnow: Conduct and attribution.

whatCanGoWrong: Each resolution is recorded with when and by whom; what happens when two members resolve one knock at once is not specified (Intake Doctrine section 2a).
steps.feelingRisk: Unvetted material entering the record as if vouched.
openInThisStep: Whether the resulting capture names the doorbell as its provenance.

journeyExperience.journey: (g) A review copy round trip with an outside reviewer
journeyExperience.spans: days to weeks; owner, editors, outside recipient

steps.step: Editors draft; owner grants a named recipient
steps.whatTheyKnow: What is missing (the publish gates' own answer).
steps.feelingRisk: Advance copy mistaken for a publication.

steps.step: Recipient reads, comments, acknowledges the statement
steps.whatTheyKnow: The statement first, then what the case leaves out, then what is still needed.
whatCanGoWrong: Grant revoked or draft moved: dead answer.
Draft edited after reading: the answer names the latest change (review R17).
steps.feelingRisk: The copy changed after the reviewer read it.

steps.step: Editors revise; the owner publishes, naming the draft
steps.whatTheyKnow: Acknowledgements bound to this case identity.
whatCanGoWrong: Readings on a draft not named at publish are counted UNDETERMINED, never listed (Publication section 3 rule 13).
steps.feelingRisk: Attributing a reading to a case its reader never saw.

journeyExperience.spans: weeks; statutory clock; the office outside

steps.step: Make the request under its governing law
steps.whatTheyKnow: The law and its deadline (from the profile).
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Record it sent; state the clock
steps.whatTheyKnow: Statutory days, holidays.
whatCanGoWrong: LEASE_HELD while another member writes the action.
steps.feelingRisk: A computed date stored as fact (never: overdue is derived).

steps.step: Record what came back: records, fee quote, denial, or nothing
steps.whatTheyKnow: The ledger.
whatCanGoWrong: No response: recorded as its own entry.
steps.feelingRisk: A non-response read as agreement (a declared inference bias can block that reading).
steps.src: actions R15-R22; Declared Bias (inference example); Case Making section 8

journeyExperience.journey: (i) A source changes after a case is published

steps.step: Monitoring detects modified or removed
steps.whatTheyKnow: Baseline and new bytes.
whatCanGoWrong: Shell match never reads unchanged; governed refusal is not the source failing.
steps.feelingRisk: Detecting change is mechanical; what it means is not.

steps.step: Members see affected findings and version notices
steps.whatTheyKnow: Causes derived on read.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Adopt newer, keep earlier, record re-evaluation.
whatCanGoWrong: Withheld dependents stated without a count.
steps.feelingRisk: Silence claimed without reading ('unaffected').

steps.step: Reopen and publish a new edition
steps.whatTheyKnow: The published edition keeps answering.
whatCanGoWrong: COMPLETENESS_CARRIED_FORWARD if the statement is byte-identical.
steps.feelingRisk: Readers relying on the old edition; supersession is surfaced, not pushed.
steps.src: promotion R21-R26; case-authoring R10; conformance R10; filings R12; DEC-12

journeyExperience.journey: (j) Adding a third administrator, or removing one

steps.step: Propose the new administrator
steps.whatTheyKnow: Current count; votes needed.
whatCanGoWrong: Created proposed at two or more administrators.
steps.feelingRisk: 'Pending approval' instead of '2 of 3' hides the arithmetic.
steps.src: membership R5, R14; Interaction Constructs section B

steps.step: Endorse, or vote to remove with a reason
steps.whatTheyKnow: Tally, who must still act, what carries.
whatCanGoWrong: ROOT_OF_TRUST (founder cannot be removed; hosting account is the remedy).
A bearer credential cannot cast a vote (control-plane R14).
steps.feelingRisk: Being outvoted without seeing the denominator.

openQuestions.question: How is a contradiction presented to a member, and what does resolving one look like (both sides in the record's words; a resolution that records its kind and may promote double-speak into a finding)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Contradictions are 'golden nuggets' the system exists to find; in our own record they carry a duty to resolve. PRESENT and RESOLVE are undesigned and nothing shows a candidate to a member.

openQuestions.question: How does a knock become part of the record: what does 'pulled' commit a member to, and does the capture name the doorbell as its provenance?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: It is the only route in for whistleblowers and outsiders, and unvetted material must never look vouched for.

openQuestions.question: Does a project show a stage (forming, investigating, matured, closed) and a work-product readiness ladder, and how?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The Roadmap's project workspace has phase bars; the lifecycle and readiness ladder exist in canon only and no requirement holds them.

openQuestions.question: What are the five steps of the publication ceremony, and what does the placeholder say until it is built?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Publication is the only irreversible act and the ceremony is the safeguard; its process is deferred (DEC-33).

openQuestions.question: Does the project workspace show grades and strength, given the legacy UI hides grades there (UI-16 note) while canon says strength is shown rather than hidden?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Showing strength is the core defence against over-claiming; hiding it in the place members work may undercut that.
openQuestions.whereTheCanonStops: Case Making section 4a; legacy app.html (not canon)

openQuestions.question: What is the one visual treatment and voice of UNDETERMINED, and how does it differ from 'withheld', 'unrated', 'not looked' and 'refused'?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: It appears in many unrelated places and must be identical everywhere, or members learn to ignore it.

openQuestions.question: How does the rung ladder look and feel so a member senses weight before acting, especially the attested and irreversible rungs?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Weight flattening is named as a doctrine failure wearing a usability improvement.

openQuestions.question: Where does a member record why something is (or is not) significant enough to escalate, given no significance field is allowed?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Significance is the point where policy preference most tempts; requirements forbid scores, so the judgment lives only in acts.
openQuestions.whereTheCanonStops: Functional Architecture Layer 2 Function 4; conformance R8

openQuestions.question: What does the action plan surface (S11) look like: options, dependencies, deadlines, resources, outcome branches, declined options, and support status on every element?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Impacting has no working process; a plan that hid a hypothetical premise would be the over-claiming failure.

openQuestions.question: What does the assistant dialog look like on each surface, and how is 'the machine did the looking, you do the concluding' made felt?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The assistant is one way in everywhere and must never appear to conclude; the pilot flow and wizard are unbuilt.

openQuestions.question: What does a newcomer learn first, and how do starter materials and onboarding fit a first session?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Design Requirement 11 requires usability within one session by someone with no civic experience; starter materials are not started.

openQuestions.question: How are the five trust levels (our work, independently verified, meets standards, not yet evaluated, flagged) shown on information from other groups?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Trust signals must be ambient and travel with data; no requirement holds the indicator.

openQuestions.question: How is a member told a capture's grade at the moment of capture (DEC-51), and what co-attestation would be worth?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The belief about what a capture is worth forms at capture; the note is currently discarded before the member sees it.

openQuestions.question: How does the queue avoid nagging (DEC-69) while making sure obligations with clocks are not missed?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Respect for members is a requirement; so are deadlines (Operational Principle 3).

openQuestions.question: What are the empty and loading states across surfaces, especially long waits (renders deferred, capture requests hours away, statutory clocks of days)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Canon names waits but no treatment; an empty state can be mistaken for 'nothing to do' or 'could not read'.

openQuestions.question: What accessibility level and which languages must the member surfaces and published output meet?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Canon names phones and print only; a civic product's public output may need to reach non-English readers and assistive technology users.

openQuestions.question: How does a subject named in a case (an office, or an official in role) see and respond, and how is the publisher's right-of-reply declaration shown?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Right of reply is a declaration, not a gate (DEC-13); a response returns as captured evidence, not a channel.

openQuestions.question: How is a correction made visible to people who relied on an earlier edition (pull, never push)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Media and peers rely on cases; a published hash answers forever.

openQuestions.question: How is attribution chosen and shown (group, project, cover, name), including off-the-record sources, without making pseudonymous work look weaker?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Attribution surface is designed in Program B and unbuilt; an identity badge would be a structural prior against a class of publisher.

openQuestions.question: How are declared bias statements shown to readers so that a lens is weighable, not a weapon (the two-audience choice)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Opponents will quote the manifest; the malformedness rule makes it survivable only if shown well.

openQuestions.question: How are hunches shown during investigation (temporary high grade) versus in strength (inert), and how is clearing one before publication presented?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: A hunch inflates a grade; a case over an uncleared hunch states a strength that is not true.

openQuestions.question: What does a group see when it names its cases for audiences with different standards of proof (journalist vs lawyer), given the catalogue of standards by audience is owed?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Without it the project bar is 'a number a project picks'.

openQuestions.question: How is an out-of-view ancestor or withheld dependent phrased so it states incompleteness and nothing else?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: DEC-36 is absolute on identity and detail; a later session must not 'fix' it toward silence.

openQuestions.question: How does the product present the difference between the working side and the published side so a member always knows which side of the fence they are on?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The privacy fence is architectural; working and published material must never share surface ambiguity.

openQuestions.question: How are declared flows (progressions) and their deltas drawn so the analytic product (declared vs observed flow) is visible, and our own missed deadlines are never shown as findings about the world?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The delta is the product; conflating plans with progressions converts a management fact into evidence.
openQuestions.whereTheCanonStops: NOTIFICATIONS.md (D-128); Case Making action plan section 3

openQuestions.question: What does the knocker, and the member at the doorbell, see when the rate bound is hit (no translation yet, D-508)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: A refusal must teach; a 429 is a claim that needs a count behind it.

openQuestions.question: How is the founder / root-of-trust responsibility explained, given custody is unmodelled (DEC-2 deferred)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Losing or leaking it has costs the group should understand at claim time.

openQuestions.question: How are the three queue classes presented differently while remaining one queue (findings compose into cases, obligations into a flow model, conditions into status on the thing)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Bob ruled they deserve different treatment; each has its own home beyond the queue.

openQuestions.question: How does the directory, cross-group discussion and 'working on' signalling appear, if at all, inside CivicOS?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Design Requirements 9-10 require them; no module holds them.

openQuestions.question: How are strength, grades and look states explained to the public reader at progressively deeper levels, and in print?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Readers know least; print loses interactivity and must carry the full narrative.
